title: Using a Robot to Print the Lexicographically Smallest String
summary: Given a string s and an empty string t, use a robot to remove characters from s or t and write the lexicographically smallest string possible on paper by following specific operations until both strings are empty.
statement: Given a string s and an empty string t, use a robot to remove characters from s or t and write the lexicographically smallest string possible on paper by following specific operations until both strings are empty.
constraints: Process source string s from left to right and maintain a robot stack t.
An operation either moves the next source character onto t or pops t’s last character onto the output.
Use all characters and return the lexicographically smallest output possible.
hints: Count characters still unprocessed in the source.
After pushing one character, advance the smallest remaining-letter pointer past exhausted counts.
Pop while the stack top is no larger than the smallest character still available later.
A larger top should wait for a smaller future character, while an eligible top cannot be improved by waiting; this greedy decision fixes the smallest possible next output.
editorial: A larger top should wait for a smaller future character, while an eligible top cannot be improved by waiting; this greedy decision fixes the smallest possible next output.

tests.explanation: Push until a is available, output a, then pop both z characters to obtain azz.
After pushing b and a, output a and b before processing c, producing abc.
